name: internal_laminar_and_curved_nu
title: Internal laminar convection and curved ducts: Nusselt-number correlations (function library)
summary: Ten EES FUNCTIONs returning the Nusselt number of single-phase internal flow at low Reynolds number or in non-circular/curved ducts: fully developed laminar pipe flow at constant wall temperature (3.66) and constant heat flux (48/11), laminar thermal entry region (Hausen, Sieder-Tate, Baehr-Stephan), laminar rectangular duct (Shah-London), and turbulent spiral (Morimoto-Hotta) and helical coils (Mori-Nakayama, Schmidt, Xin-Ebadian). The heat-transfer coefficient follows from h = Nu*k/Dh and is left to the caller.

authors: R. K. Shah and A. L. London (Shah-London rectangular-duct correlation)
E. Morimoto and K. Hotta (Morimoto-Hotta spiral correlation)
Y. Mori and W. Nakayama (Mori-Nakayama helical correlation)
R. C. Xin and M. A. Ebadian (Xin-Ebadian helical correlation)
E. N. Sieder and G. E. Tate (Sieder-Tate entry-region correlation)
H. D. Baehr and K. Stephan (Baehr-Stephan entry-region correlation)
origin.notes: ht 1.2.0, commit 85e0ee6 (2025-12-07), file ht/conv_internal.py, MIT license, Copyright (C) 2016 Caleb Bell. The scientific basis of each correlation is the original paper or book cited in its function comment block (in most cases as given in Bergman, Lavine, Incropera & DeWitt, Introduction to Heat Transfer, 6E, Wiley, 2011). Translation published under the CoolSolve_Library MIT license (decision D3).

verification.reference: doctest values of ht 1.2.0 ht/conv_internal.py (case A) and additional values computed with the same ht functions in a throw-away virtualenv (case B); 21 output values in total
verification.notes: compare_solution.py: 21 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); largest relative deviation 3.2e-13 (Nu_helical_Schmidt_B), i.e. round-off only.
